definicio: A small piece of ownership in a company. If you own shares, you're a part-owner: you gain if the company becomes worth more, and you may receive dividends.
exemple: If a company has 1,000 shares and you own 10, you own 1% of it.

definicio: The part of its profits that a company shares out among its shareholders, usually in cash.
exemple: A company paying €0.50 per share gives you €50 if you own 100.

definicio: A single number that sums up how a group of listed companies is doing. It tells you at a glance whether the market is going up or down.
exemple: The Ibex 35 tracks the 35 most traded companies on the Spanish stock exchange.

definicio: A fund that buys all the companies in an index and trades on the stock market like a share. With a single purchase, you invest in many companies at once.
exemple: The EWP ETF tracks the Spanish stock market: it's what The Daily Spread uses to follow it.

definicio: A pot of money from many savers, managed by a professional who invests it in shares, bonds or other assets.
exemple: With €100 you can own a slice of a fund that holds shares in hundreds of companies.

definicio: Earning interest on the interest you've already earned. Over time, the effect snowballs.
exemple: €100 at 5% a year becomes €105 after the first year and €110.25 after the second: in year two you also earn interest on the first year's €5.

definicio: The general rise in prices. If inflation is 5%, the same money buys 5% less than it did a year ago.
exemple: A €1 loaf of bread now costs €1.05.

definicio: The Consumer Price Index (IPC in Spanish): Spain's official measure of inflation. The national statistics office (INE) calculates it every month from a basket of goods a typical household buys.
exemple: When CPI is said to be 4.9%, it means the basket costs 4.9% more than a year ago.

definicio: Inflation excluding energy and fresh food, whose prices swing a lot. It gives a better picture of the underlying price trend.
exemple: If electricity prices spike one month, headline inflation jumps, but core inflation barely moves.

definicio: The price of money: what you pay to borrow it or what you earn for lending it.
exemple: A €10,000 loan at 6% a year costs you about €600 in interest in the first year.

definicio: The European Central Bank, which sets the official interest rate for the euro area to keep inflation close to 2%.
exemple: If inflation is too high, the ECB raises rates to cool spending and lending.

definicio: The Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States. Its interest rate decisions move stock markets around the world.
exemple: When the Fed raises rates, the dollar often strengthens and stocks fall.

definicio: The interest rate at which European banks lend money to each other. Most variable-rate mortgages in Spain are linked to it.
exemple: If the Euribor rises by one point, the monthly payment on a €150,000 variable-rate mortgage over 25 years goes up by about €80.

definicio: The fixed margin the bank adds to the Euribor on a variable-rate mortgage. It never changes over the life of the mortgage.
exemple: With Euribor + 0.75% and the Euribor at 3.29%, you pay 4.04%.

definicio: A mortgage whose interest rate is reset every 6 or 12 months in line with the Euribor. If the Euribor rises, you pay more; if it falls, you pay less.
exemple: With a fixed-rate mortgage, by contrast, you always pay the same, whatever happens.

definicio: A loan you make to a government or a company. In return, they pay you interest and, at the end, give you your money back.
exemple: A 10-year government bond at 3% pays you €30 a year for every €1,000 you put in.

definicio: A short-term loan to the Spanish state (3, 6, 9 or 12 months). It's one of the safest investments there is.
exemple: You buy a bill for about €970 and a year later the state pays you back €1,000.

definicio: Leaving money with a bank for a fixed period in exchange for an agreed interest rate. Up to €100,000 is protected by a deposit guarantee scheme.
exemple: A €5,000 deposit at 2.5% for one year earns you €125 before tax.

definicio: The annual percentage rate (TAE in Spain): the true yearly cost or return of a product, fees included. It's how you compare offers.
exemple: Between two loans, the one with the lower APR is the cheaper one.

definicio: What you gain (or lose) on an investment, as a percentage of what you put in.
exemple: If you invest €1,000 and a year later you have €1,080, your return is 8%.

definicio: Your return after subtracting inflation. It tells you whether you can really buy more than before.
exemple: Earning 3% with inflation at 4.9% means losing almost 2% of purchasing power.

definicio: How sharply and how often an investment's price goes up and down. The more volatile it is, the higher the short-term risk.
exemple: A tech stock can move 5% in a day; a government bond, hardly at all.

definicio: Spreading your money across many different investments so that if one goes badly, you don't lose everything.
exemple: Better to own shares in 50 companies across different sectors than all in just one.

definicio: What a company is worth on the stock market: the share price multiplied by the number of shares.
exemple: 100 million shares at €50 each make a market capitalisation of €5bn.

definicio: How many times its annual profit a company is worth on the stock market (share price divided by earnings per share). It helps you tell whether it's expensive or cheap.
exemple: A P/E of 20 means you pay €20 for every euro of annual profit.

definicio: The company's profit divided by the number of shares.
exemple: A company that earns €1bn and has 500 million shares has earnings per share of €2.

definicio: The accounts listed companies publish every three months. If they fall short of expectations, the share price usually drops.
exemple: Alphabet fell more than 12% in a day because its sales came in below forecasts.

definicio: When a private company starts selling its shares on the stock market so that anyone can buy them. Also known as an IPO.
exemple: Anthropic has filed to go public under the ticker ANT.

definicio: When a company that isn't yet listed raises money from investors in exchange for a share of ownership.
exemple: If someone puts $30bn into a company valued at $1.25tn, they get a little over 2% of it.

definicio: A bull market is a long stretch of rising prices; a bear market is a fall of 20% or more from the peak.
exemple: The names come from how each animal attacks: the bull thrusts its horns upwards, the bear swipes downwards.

definicio: How many units of one currency another one is worth.
exemple: With the euro at $1.117, €100 gets you $111.70.

definicio: Gross domestic product: the value of everything a country produces in a year. If it grows, the economy is doing well.
exemple: US GDP growing at an annualised 3.4% means the economy is expanding strongly.

definicio: When a country's GDP falls for two quarters in a row. It usually comes with higher unemployment and lower spending.
How quickly you can turn an investment into cash without losing value.
exemple: A current account is fully liquid; a flat, hardly at all: selling it takes months.

definicio: The average closing price over the last few days (20, 50…), recalculated every day. It helps you see the trend without the daily noise.
exemple: If the price is above its 50-day average, the recent trend is upwards.

definicio: A way of drawing each day's price: the body shows the opening and closing prices, and the thin lines show the high and the low.
exemple: A blue candle (in our search tool) means the price closed that day above where it opened.

definicio: How many shares were bought and sold in a session. A move on high volume carries more weight.
How much more a country pays than Germany to borrow for 10 years. It measures how much investors trust that country.
exemple: If the Spanish bond pays 3.2% and the German one 2.5%, the risk premium is 70 basis points.

definicio: One hundredth of a percentage point. 100 basis points make 1%.
exemple: If a rate goes from 2.85% to 3.03%, it has risen by 18 basis points.
